name: Sherry Whitfield

five_sec.what_is_it: HelloFresh. The company that shipped me a box I didn't order.
five_sec.who_for: New customers they can lock into a weekly subscription.
five_sec.trust_why: 'Open A Box To Reveal Your Offer!' A spin-to-win pop-up is the first thing I see. That's a red flag, not a welcome.
five_sec.next_step: Skip the offer and scroll straight to the fine print.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Three green HelloFresh boxes on the pop-up. They ship meal kits.

full_page.what_stopped_me: The asterisk. The offer needs 'a qualifying auto-renewing subscription,' the 'Free for Life' item ends when you cancel, and shipping is charged after the first box. Prices only after a zip code.
full_page.whats_missing: A price without a zip code. Plain renewal and cutoff dates on the page.

HF.quote: 'Free Breakfast for Life' requires a 'qualifying auto-renewing subscription' and is void the day you cancel. I've lived this one already.

five_sec.what_is_it: A meal-planning app that suggests dinners.
five_sec.who_for: Parents with the mental load of dinner.
five_sec.trust_why: 'Trusted by 90,000+ families' with no source. The main button is 'Letter from the CEO,' which is not a next step.
five_sec.next_step: Find the pricing and the cancel terms.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The phone shows food photos and 'I've picked out meals for you.' Doesn't say whether anything ships.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Two different stories on price. The meal page says a 1-month trial with 'prices available when you download the app.' The pricing page bills per message with $0.30 top-ups.
full_page.whats_missing: One consistent price. What the trial turns into. Whether a card is needed.

OL.quote: The FAQ says 'prices are available when you download the app,' then the pricing page has $0.30 message top-ups. I'd need a spreadsheet just for Ollie.

five_sec.what_is_it: A dinner planner that texts the family to vote and fills your Instacart or Walmart cart.
five_sec.who_for: Families with a lot of opinions and no time.
five_sec.trust_why: 'Start free, no card needed' is on the first screen, and 'We don't deliver food' tells me they've heard the confusion. Still an unknown brand.
five_sec.next_step: Skip the hero, go to pricing and the FAQ.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Bold line: 'We don't deliver food. We plan your week and send your grocery list.'

full_page.what_stopped_me: Very little. The terms pass. My reservations: 'over 500 families have signed up' is a count, not a review, and the sign-up page adds a weekly email with 'the occasional kitchen pick,' which is marketing.
full_page.whats_missing: Outside reviews or an App Store rating. Harris Teeter by name (is it the Kroger cart?). A screenshot of the cancel button in Account.

DD.quote: 'Your free Family days need no card, so there is nothing to cancel.' That's the sentence eMeals and HelloFresh never wrote. Now show me outside reviews.

five_sec.what_is_it: A recipe organizer and meal-planning app.
five_sec.who_for: People who already keep recipes and like to plan.
five_sec.trust_why: 'Free Trial - no card required!' on the first screen, plus real app-store ratings.
five_sec.next_step: Read the pricing page billing questions.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: App-store buttons and a person writing a list. It's software.

full_page.what_stopped_me: Excellent terms, but I'd still be the one picking every meal on a volleyball night. And then a countdown clock for 'our only sale of the year.' Pick a lane.
full_page.whats_missing: A way for the kids to weigh in. Something that plans for me.

PTE.quote: 'We don't auto-bill when your year ends unless you choose to.' That's the sentence I look for. Then a countdown sale clock. Pick a lane.

five_sec.what_is_it: eMeals. The one that renewed me without notice.
five_sec.who_for: Families who want weekly meal plans.
five_sec.trust_why: My own history. And the first screen is a video with no terms in sight.
five_sec.next_step: Look for the price and renewal terms.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: I know from using it: it's plans and a shopping list, not food.

full_page.what_stopped_me: No price on the page, no renewal terms, a 'LIMITED TIME' pop-up asking for my email, and 'No commitment. Cancel anytime.' I've heard that before.
full_page.whats_missing: Price, whether a card is required, what happens on day 15.

EM.quote: 'No commitment. Cancel anytime.' That's what I read last time, right before eMeals renewed me without a word. Still no price, still no renewal date.

dd_offer.why: It answers my three questions directly: no card for the 14 days, nothing to cancel, you go back to Free. The FAQ 'Will I be charged by surprise?' is the right question to ask.
dd_offer.expect_day_15: Family features turn off and I'm on the free plan. No card on file, so no charge. If I had added a card, I'd get an email 3 days before.

head_to_head.reason: It's the only one with no card, a free plan underneath, and a written answer to 'what happens on day 15', plus the kids can vote.

HF.reason: No pop-up game and no auto-renewing box.

OL.reason: One clear price instead of message counts and top-ups.

PTE.reason: Both have honest terms; DinnerDrop also plans for me and lets the family weigh in.

EM.reason: DinnerDrop shows the price and the day-15 rule. eMeals shows neither.

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Pricing page (/start), right under the Family card: an App Store rating or link to outside reviews, plus a screenshot of the one-tap cancel in Account. 'Over 500 families have signed up' tells me size, not satisfaction.
